name: Edinburgh
operatingHours: Edinburgh Trams (one line, Newhaven–Leith–Princes Street–Haymarket–Airport) run ~5:00 AM–~12:00 AM Mon–Sat and ~6:30 AM–~12:00 AM Sun, every ~7 min by day and 10–15 min in the evening. No metro; Lothian buses fill the gaps and night buses run all night.
fareInfo: City Zone single £2.40, return £4.60, DAYticket £6.00 (from 22 Feb 2026); tap a contactless card or phone on the platform reader and daily capping applies (~£5.70). Airport Zone tickets are extra: single ~£7.50, return ~£10.50, Network DAY £14.00. Lothian bus tickets are valid on trams in the City Zone (not to the airport). Buy before boarding: at stop machines, with the Transport for Edinburgh app, or by contactless.

sights.name: The Real Mary King's Close
sights.note: Guided tours led by costumed characters through a warren of 17th-century streets sealed beneath the City Chambers on the Royal Mile.
sights.hours: Tours ~9:30 AM–9:00 PM daily (shorter in winter)

sights.name: Edinburgh Castle
sights.note: The fortress on an extinct volcano above the city, home to the Scottish Crown Jewels, the Stone of Destiny and the one o'clock gun.
sights.hours: 9:30 AM–6:00 PM Apr–Sep, 9:30 AM–5:00 PM Oct–Mar; last entry 1 h before close

sights.name: Arthur's Seat
sights.note: The 251 m summit of an ancient volcano in Holyrood Park, a steep 45-minute hike from the Palace for a sweeping view over the city and the Firth of Forth.

sights.name: Royal Yacht Britannia
sights.note: The Queen's former floating residence, moored at Ocean Terminal in Leith, where you walk from the royal apartments to the engine room and crew quarters.
sights.hours: ~9:30 AM–4:30 PM daily (to ~5:00 PM in summer)

sights.name: National Museum of Scotland
sights.note: A free museum covering Scottish history, world cultures, natural history and science, with Dolly the sheep and a rooftop terrace view of the castle.

sights.name: Johnnie Walker Princes Street
sights.note: An eight-floor whisky experience in a former department store at the west end of Princes Street, with tasting tours and a rooftop bar facing the castle.
sights.hours: Tours ~10:00 AM–8:00 PM daily; rooftop bar later

sights.name: Camera Obscura and World of Illusions
sights.note: A Victorian rooftop camera obscura that projects live views of the city, above five floors of hands-on optical illusions just below the castle.

sights.name: Palace of Holyroodhouse
sights.note: The King's official residence in Scotland at the foot of the Royal Mile, with Mary Queen of Scots' chambers and the ruined Holyrood Abbey.
sights.hours: 9:30 AM–6:00 PM Apr–Oct, 9:30 AM–4:30 PM Nov–Mar (closed Tue–Wed in winter and during royal visits)

sights.name: Royal Mile
sights.note: The Old Town's spine, running downhill from the castle to Holyrood past closes, churches, pubs and street performers.
sights.hours: Street, always open; shops ~10:00 AM–6:00 PM

sights.name: Calton Hill
sights.note: A short climb from Princes Street to the unfinished National Monument and Nelson Monument, the classic free sunset view over the city.

sights.name: The Scotch Whisky Experience
sights.note: A barrel-ride introduction to whisky-making next to the castle esplanade, ending in a tasting beside a vast collection of bottles.

sights.name: Dean Village
sights.note: A former mill village of stone houses tucked in the Water of Leith gorge, a ten-minute walk from the West End.

sights.name: Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh
sights.note: Seventy acres of gardens north of Stockbridge with a rock garden, Chinese hillside and skyline views; entry to the gardens is free.
sights.hours: 10:00 AM–6:00 PM Mar–Sep, to 5:00 PM Feb/Oct, to 4:00 PM Nov–Jan; glasshouses closed for restoration

sights.name: Princes Street Gardens
sights.note: Gardens in the old loch valley beneath the castle, with the Ross Fountain and the Christmas market in winter.

sights.name: St Giles' Cathedral
sights.note: The High Kirk of Edinburgh on the Royal Mile, with a crown-shaped spire and the carved Thistle Chapel; entry is free.
sights.hours: Mon–Sat 10:00 AM–6:00 PM (to 5:00 PM in winter), Sun 1:00–5:00 PM

sights.name: Scottish National Gallery
sights.note: A free gallery on the Mound holding Scottish and European masters from Raphael and Titian to Raeburn and Monet.

sights.name: Grassmarket
sights.note: An old cattle-market square under the castle crag, lined with pubs and a Saturday street-food market, and the bottom of colourful Victoria Street.
sights.hours: Square, always open; pubs to ~1:00 AM

sights.name: Scott Monument
sights.note: A 61 m Gothic spire on Princes Street honouring Sir Walter Scott; 287 narrow steps lead to galleries looking over Waverley and the Old Town.
sights.hours: ~10:00 AM–7:00 PM Apr–Sep, ~10:00 AM–4:00 PM Oct–Mar

railStations.name: Edinburgh Waverley
railStations.note: Edinburgh's main station in the valley between the Old and New Towns: LNER, Lumo and CrossCountry to London King's Cross (~4h20m), Avanti to Birmingham, ScotRail to Glasgow (~50 min), Stirling, Inverness and Aberdeen, plus the Caledonian Sleeper. The Princes Street and St Andrew Square tram stops are a 3–5 min walk up the steps.
railStations.hours: Station open ~4:30 AM–~1:00 AM; trains run to individual timetables. Trams ~5:00 AM–~12:00 AM.

railStations.name: Haymarket
railStations.note: Edinburgh's second station, 1.5 km west of Waverley: most ScotRail services to Glasgow, Fife, Aberdeen and Inverness and many LNER/CrossCountry trains stop here, and the Haymarket tram stop is right outside.
railStations.hours: Station open ~5:00 AM–~12:30 AM; trains run to individual timetables. Trams ~5:00 AM–~12:00 AM.

airports.name: Edinburgh Airport
airports.transitNote: The tram (on the map) runs from the stop outside the terminal to Haymarket in ~25 min and Princes Street in ~35 min, every ~7 min (Airport Zone fare ~£7.50 single). Airlink 100 bus to Waverley takes ~30 min and runs 24 h (not on the map).
airports.hours: Trams: first ~5:00 AM (~6:30 AM Sun), last ~11:45 PM. Airlink 100 runs 24 h.
